hints: Focus on exactly when sister chromatids are supposed to separate, and which stage comes just before that moment.
Remember colchicine prevents spindle fibres from working, so think about what the spindle is needed for at the equator of the cell.
walkthrough:
**Recall the order of mitosis**

Great start, let us get the sequence clear in your head. Mitosis runs in order: prophase, then metaphase, then anaphase, then telophase.

Think of it as: condense, line up, pull apart, then rebuild.

**Pinpoint where separation happens**

Sister chromatids line up on the metaphase plate during metaphase. They are then pulled apart to opposite poles during anaphase by spindle fibres.

No working spindle means no pulling force.

**Apply colchicine to the sequence**

Prophase can still finish because chromosomes can still condense. The cell then enters metaphase and tries to line up chromosomes.

But without a working spindle, it cannot complete metaphase and cannot move on into anaphase. It gets stuck at metaphase.

options.A: Anaphase is the separation itself, so if separation is blocked the cell never properly starts anaphase.
options.B: The cell enters metaphase but without spindle action it cannot align and trigger separation, so metaphase is reached but not completed.
options.C: Prophase happens before any spindle pulling is needed, so chromosome condensation completes normally.
options.D: Telophase is much later when nuclei reform, so the cell never gets that far if stuck at metaphase.
